correctness.rationale: The exact directed-cycle resolvent has diagonal (1+s*r_i)^-1/(1-product(s*r_j/(1+s*r_j))). Its rational numerator 2N_i-D has coefficients e_k(r_without_i)-r_i*e_{k-1}(r_without_i). Newton inequalities give decreasing adjacent elementary-symmetric ratios and hence at most one positive-to-negative sign change. The leading sign is determined by inverse-rate stationary mass. This establishes an exact single simple positive root for each obstructing diagonal and no root for other diagonals. Ordering by r_i makes a maximum-rate state decisive; a strict product monotonicity proves the sharp homogeneous upper envelope and vanishing-rate lower infimum. Replayed finite exact-rational checks support identities, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The general Cayley diagonal-resolvent criterion is already known and is expressly credited. The closest full published-finding corpus proof establishes one-crossing using reversibility and explicitly does not classify the nonreversible case. Its hypotheses cannot imply a theorem for directed cycles of length >=3, which violate detailed balance. Inspected published primary sources address general absolute monotonicity, Cayley classes, centered-difference advection and symmetric heat operators, none providing the precise heterogeneous directed-cycle polynomial, rate-order independence, strict no-recovery law or sharp fixed-M bounds.
residual_risks: A specialized cyclic-resolvent/implicit upwind paper might already imply the elementary-symmetric formula and its one-crossing and extremal laws; primary sources located and read do not settle publication priority absolutely.
The claim is restricted to one-way finite directed cycles and strictly positive rates; comparison with nonlinear positivity or arbitrary nonreversible chains is inapplicable.

value.rationale: Sharp positivity intervals for nonreversible transport discretizations matter for invariant-region numerical analysis. The result gives a fully general all-cycle-size, all-positive-rate classification, a finite elementary-symmetric root computation, a non-obvious rate-order invariance principle, and sharp best/worst positivity horizons at fixed largest rate. It is not a mere restatement of the general Cayley identity: sign-variation and extrema require distinct arguments and answer a natural fixed-generator gap.
